headline: Capricor announced on November 20, 2026 that it received a Complete Response Letter on its resubmitted BLA for deramiocel in Duchenne muscular dystrophy; the goal date was November 22, and the release does not date the letter.
pdufa_note: Capricor announced on the evening of November 20, 2026 (7:55 PM ET) that it received a Complete Response Letter for its resubmitted BLA for deramiocel, its cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (Capricor's announcement). Per Capricor, the letter states that the FDA does not consider the data sufficient to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness and cites certain other clinical deficiencies; Capricor said it is reviewing the letter and will share next steps after its evaluation. The PDUFA goal date was November 22, 2026, moved from August 22 after a major amendment to the application (Capricor, August 24, 2026). The release does not state the letter's own date, so no early or late margin is given. This is deramiocel's second Complete Response Letter; the first was announced on July 11, 2025 (CAPR, July 11, 2025). A Complete Response Letter means the FDA will not approve the application in its present form; the sponsor can resubmit.

indication: Generalized myasthenia gravis in adults who are anti-AChR antibody positive
headline: The FDA approved Klygefa (gefurulimab-gaks) on November 13, 2026 for adults with generalized myasthenia gravis who are anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody positive; AstraZeneca announced the approval on November 16.
pdufa_note: The FDA's approval letter for BLA 761488, signed November 13, 2026 (FDA letter), covers Klygefa (gefurulimab-gaks) for adults with generalized myasthenia gravis who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive. The letter states that the application was received on November 13, 2025, and it approves a REMS because of the risk of serious meningococcal infections. AstraZeneca announced the approval on November 16, 2026 and describes once-weekly subcutaneous self-administration by autoinjector (AstraZeneca, November 16, 2026). Per AstraZeneca, in the Phase III PREVAIL trial (260 patients) the MG-ADL total score improved more than with placebo at week 26 (treatment difference -1.6, p<0.0001). We hold no publicly disclosed PDUFA goal date for this application, so no early or late margin is given.
